subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: MRKH, Androgen Insensitivity and Kallmann Syndrome

steps.tx: Absent uterus and upper vagina with normal ovaries in a forty six XX woman is **MRKH** in amenorrhoea practice. Breasts and pubic hair are fully developed, separating it from androgen insensitivity by hair alone. The vagina is a shallow dimple. It affects about one in five thousand female births and is the second commonest cause of primary amenorrhoea.
steps.say: MRKH absents the uterus with normal hair, separating it from androgen insensitivity.

steps.tx: Complete resistance to androgens in a forty six XY individual giving female phenotype without uterus is **androgen insensitivity syndrome**. Breasts develop from aromatised oestrogen but pubic hair is scant. Testes sit in the abdomen or inguinal canal. Pubic hair is sparse or absent because hair follicles also resist androgens, the clue that separates it from MRKH at examination.
steps.say: Androgen insensitivity gives female phenotype with scant hair and abdominal testes.

steps.tx: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with absent smell from failed GnRH neuron migration is **Kallmann syndrome**. Puberty never starts and anosmia is the diagnostic gift. Pulsatile GnRH or gonadotropins restore fertility completely. The gene defect is in KAL1 and related genes, and affected boys may have a missing kidney on scan.
steps.say: Kallmann syndrome pairs absent puberty with anosmia from failed GnRH migration.

steps.tx: Inguinal herniae in girls may contain testes, so hernia in a phenotypic girl prompts **karyotype awareness**. Many AIS cases declare exactly this way in childhood. Repair surgeons send gonadal tissue for histology when found. A hernia sac containing a firm oval gonad in a baby girl should be photographed, sampled and never simply removed.
steps.say: Hernia in a phenotypic girl may reveal testes and declare androgen insensitivity.

steps.tx: Gonadectomy is timed by diagnosis. In complete androgen insensitivity the testes stay until after puberty so aromatised androgen can supply oestrogen for breast growth, then come out as germ-cell tumour risk rises. Partial insensitivity has a higher risk and earlier removal. A hernia in a phenotypic girl may hide a testis, and **karyotype awareness** means the gonad is photographed and sampled, not simply discarded. Ovaries stay in Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome.
steps.say: Gonadectomy is timed by diagnosis. Partial insensitivity has a higher risk and earlier removal. vis.alt: Timing chart for gonadectomy in androgen insensitivity versus ovaries retained in MRKH
vis.caption: Gonadectomy is placed after puberty in complete androgen insensitivity, earlier when tumour risk is higher, and omitted in MRKH. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Gonadectomy timing in complete AIS balances tumour risk against puberty induction by endogenous hormones, termed **gonadectomy timing**. Many now defer until after puberty completes spontaneously. Shared decision making with the patient is essential. Tumour risk before puberty is low, near one percent, rising slowly afterwards, which permits the delay.
steps.say: Gonadectomy timing in AIS often defers until after spontaneous puberty completes.

steps.tx: Partial androgen insensitivity gives ambiguous genitalia at birth and a spectrum, grouped as **PAIS spectrum**. Sex assignment needs multidisciplinary teams and family time. Karyotype, hormones and receptor studies guide without rushing. Gender identity is usually female in complete insensitivity and more variable in partial forms.
steps.say: Partial androgen insensitivity gives ambiguous genitalia needing multidisciplinary time.

steps.tx: A karyotype is not news to be given in a corridor between other patients. **Sensitive disclosure** of Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome, or of androgen insensitivity, is arranged with gynaecology, endocrinology and psychology in the room, in the words the person has asked to hear, and across more than one visit. Complete androgen insensitivity is usually a female gender identity. Partial forms need time before any operation is even discussed. Who else is told, and whether dilatation or fertility options are wanted, is written as the person's decision.
steps.say: MRKH and androgen insensitivity are explained over more than one visit, with the team present and in the person's own terms. Complete insensitivity is usually lived as female. Surgery is not rushed, and disclosure to others is the person's choice.

vis.alt: Flowchart for explaining a new diagnosis of MRKH or androgen insensitivity, with a multidisciplinary team and staged visits.
vis.caption: Disclosure of MRKH or androgen insensitivity is shown as a staged conversation with gynaecology, endocrinology and psychology present. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Vaginal hypoplasia in AIS is managed by dilation exactly as in MRKH, a shared **dilation pathway**. Surgery is rarely needed in either condition. Psychological support accompanies both diagnoses identically. Success with dilation reaches 85 to 95 percent in supported programmes, making surgery the exception.
steps.say: Dilation pathways serve vaginal hypoplasia identically in MRKH and AIS.

steps.tx: How a diagnosis is told can matter as much as the diagnosis itself. **Sensitive disclosure** of MRKH or AIS means private setting, unhurried time, words chosen with the young woman, and follow up arranged before she leaves. Fertility, sexuality and identity questions arrive over months, not in one consultation. A single blunt conversation in a crowded clinic is remembered for decades, which is why disclosure is treated as a clinical skill and not an afterthought.
steps.say: Disclosing MRKH or AIS needs privacy, time and planned follow up. The conversation is remembered for years, so it is a clinical skill in itself.

vis.alt: Image showing a sensitive disclosure consultation with a young woman and clinician.
vis.caption: A clinician is shown talking privately and unhurriedly with a young woman at disclosure. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Disclosure of XY karyotype in AIS needs staged, supported honesty, termed **sensitive disclosure**. Historical concealment caused lasting harm when discovered accidentally. Modern practice tells the patient herself, at her pace. Information is given in writing and revisited over several visits, with a specialist nurse present.
steps.say: Sensitive disclosure tells AIS patients themselves, staged and supported.

steps.tx: Fertility differs absolutely: AIS and MRKH both need surrogacy or adoption routes, while Kallmann restores natural fertility, summarised as **fertility contrast**. Early honest framing lets families grieve and plan realistically. Uterine surrogacy using the woman own eggs is possible in MRKH, so ovarian reserve is normal and worth stating.
steps.say: Fertility contrast separates restorable Kallmann from surrogacy needing MRKH and AIS.
